findings.title: Consolation releases Moses from the refusal
findings.claim: The closing command not to grieve also functions as consolation that releases Moses from maintaining an affective tie to the refusing group.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries the supplied grief-and-consolation relation, while the wider same-surah and cross-surah non-grief returns place that command after rejection and completed warning; their contact turns the closing prohibition into a boundary-setting consolation.
findings.reader_payoff: The last sentence can be heard as a way for Moses to separate from the group's refusal without treating their consequence as unreal.
findings.containment: This does not claim that compassion disappears, that the verb means only consolation, or that the wider parallels are the same event.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run record is citable and anchored to the focus branch, but it carries a weak grade and the consolation-as-separation relation remains interpretive.
